addresses: MAJOR, visual-desktop: 'Three frames in the same round give Dana three different accounts of the one thing J6 is about — whether Amara's link is in flight — and the frame that asks her to act is the one that says both at once.'
visual-desktop: 'a pending or press-me create is the one job class no count on the screen can reach — the exact gap round 2 closed for differs and left open here.'

The round instruction, treated as fact from the code: onStudentCreated pushes the person the moment the document lands, pushPendingVisitors sweeps what that missed, and the profile button is a retry for when both have failed.
changes.change: A quick-add's create is now a job like every other job, said the same way in all three frames. The mark is the running one with an age — '→ Creating · 40s' in the warn tone on sync-students (desktop) and '→ Creating' in the row's chip line (phone), replacing '◌ No record yet' in the ink tone — and Amara is counted in In flight, which went 3 → 4. Her caption follows the family's '{what} · {who}' pattern: 'New record · Marcus Webb'. On sync-blocked the identity chip is '→ Creating in Planning Center · 40s', the notice's glyph is → rather than ◌, its heading is 'Amara's Planning Center record is being created', and its body says who started it and that nobody has to: 'Marcus quick-added her at the door 40 seconds ago and the create went out on its own.' The guarantee under it became 'One new person, never a second copy: there is nothing to press, and the six boxes unlock the moment it lands.' **The 'Create her in Planning Center' primary is gone** — the editor's one move there is the note it says is live, and the held group's sentence now ends 'all six unlock on their own' rather than 'creating her unlocks all six'. The profile card's Planning Center line and the parent-contact line were brought into agreement too. sync-outage keeps '! Create held' unchanged in shape — the same model with the outage on top — with its tooltip corrected to say the create went out on its own and no retry helps.
changes.rationale: The three accounts were not three opinions, they were one fact told three ways, so this is a correction rather than a design choice. Once the create is a job, everything else follows mechanically: a job has a running mark, a running mark has an age, an age belongs in the running count, and a job on its way must not carry a button that fires it again — which is the operation the codebase is most careful about duplicating. Taking the button off rather than relabelling it 'Cancel this create' was deliberate: a create *can* be cancelled while queued, but on this frame it is already out, and offering a cancel would put a second guess on the same screen. The retry keeps the wording the family already has and lives only on stalled and failed.
changes.breakpoint: both — the mark, the tone, the count and the copy are identical at 390px and 1440px; only the caption is hidden below lg, as round 1 set
changes.implementation: The pending-link state stops being a standing fact on the student and becomes a `create` job in the same collection as the patch jobs: `JobChip` renders it through the ordinary `queued`/`sending` path (mark →, tone `run`, word 'Creating', age from `job.createdAt`), and `inFlight = count(state in {queued, sending, waiting, stalled})` picks it up with no special case. `◌` stays defined in the glyph map for a student with no upstream person **and no create job** — a quick-add whose create was cancelled or whose job document has been reaped — and is the only remaining use of that mark. In `StudentEditorDialog`, the branch that renders when every managed field is held drops the `Create her in Planning Center` action entirely; the create action survives only as the retry on `StudentSyncStrip` for `state in {stalled, failed}`, wording unchanged. Delete the 'open her profile to create it' tooltip string — nothing in the product should now ask a human to start a create.

addresses: MAJOR, visual-desktop: 'the merged-upstream case does not need a scene of its own — its shape is exactly differs … but differs narrates a cause that would be false and orphaned offers a move that would be dangerous.'

MAJOR, visual-phone: 'the quiet case: if the survivor already holds what Marcus typed, no difference is detected, the job reports landed, and Tally's student now points at an upstream person nobody chose.'
visual-desktop: 'orphaned should be able to say which of the two it is: deleted and re-creatable, or merged and not.'
changes.change: Merged is a branch of the `differs` strip, not a new object — and it is rendered on its own pair of files, `sync-merged--{phone,desktop}.html`, because one record can only be in one job state and putting the branch on `sync-differs` would have cost the ordinary changed-upstream case. Every class, tone, mark and layout rule is `differs`'; four things swap. (1) It fires on the id: the frame is deliberately the **silent** case — the survivor already held Chen-Ito, no value differs, and the strip is still there. (2) The actor is the merge: 'Planning Center merged Ava Chen into **Ava Chen-Ito** on Tuesday. Your correction followed the merge and landed on her, not here — she already held that surname, so nothing changed. This page now reads from her.' (3) The two-up holds people instead of values, in the same matched-cell shape with the live one ringed danger: 'NOW POINTS AT / Ava Chen-Ito / #AC377 · the survivor' against 'YOU EDITED / Ava Chen / #AC101 · merged Tue' — the ids are what carry it when the names do not. (4) The second action is not 'Send it again': it is 'Open Ava Chen-Ito' with 'Opens her in Planning Center.' under it and a quiet 'Got it' beneath, so there is no way to push a value into a record the leader has never seen. The identity block, which the phone critic pointed at as three upstream facts read at a glance, carries '≠ Merged upstream · Tue' beside the Allergies badge, and the Profile card's provenance line reads 'Read from **Ava Chen-Ito** in Planning Center, since Tuesday's merge' and links to the survivor's id. On sync-orphaned the strip now says which of the two it is — 'deleted in Planning Center on 4 August — deleted outright, not merged into anybody' — and the one-new-person guarantee was upgraded from a promise about duplicate jobs to a promise about the person: 'Planning Center holds no other record of her, so this writes one new person and never a second copy.'
changes.rationale: Both visual critics were right that the shape is `differs`, and that is exactly why it had to be a second render rather than a second component: proving the branch means showing that the same strip, the same tone, the same ≠ mark and the same two-up carry it with only the payload changed. I chose ≠ over a new mark for the same reason — what came back is not what was sent, and here the thing that came back is the person. Rendering the silent case rather than a merge-plus-difference case was the harder and more honest choice: a merge that also changes a value would have let the frame lean on the value comparison and hide the fact that the id moved. And `orphaned` had to be split in words rather than in frames, because the two causes differ only in one clause and one guarantee — but that guarantee is the difference between re-creating a deleted child and duplicating a living one.
changes.breakpoint: both, and the ordering is the one round 2 settled for differs: at lg the message and the actions sit side by side with the comparison full-width beneath; below lg it is message → comparison → actions, so the phone reader sees both people before either button.
changes.implementation: `StudentSyncStrip` gains `state='merged'`, which the drain sets when `readThroughMerges` returns a person whose id is not the id the job named — **on the id, never on the values**, so the silent case surfaces. It reuses the `differs` render path with `{observed, requested}` replaced by `{survivor: {id, name}, named: {id, name}, mergedAt}`, tone `danger`, mark `≠`, and the second action `Open {survivor.name}` linking to `people.planningcenteronline.com/people/{survivor.id}` in place of the re-send. Nothing in this state may render a control that enqueues a patch. `StudentIdentityHeader` renders the same `≠ Merged upstream · {when}` chip whenever the student's resolved person id differs from the id last stored, whether or not a job is outstanding — that is the part that protects the reader who arrives on Sunday with no job in flight. `orphaned` splits on `upstreamRecordMissing.reason`: `'deleted'` keeps the existing re-create action and the guarantee sentence; `'merged'` renders the merged branch above instead and **must not** offer re-create. In `JobChip` the glyph map is untouched: `merged` maps to `differs`' entry.

addresses: MINOR, design-phone: 'Both values and both clock times are now stated three times in three registers inside one panel — once as narrative, once as the comparison, once on the buttons. The object built to be read at a glance arrives third and lands as a recap.'
design-phone: 'the left cell's provenance wraps to two lines while the right's does not, leaving a dead band in the right cell.'
changes.change: The cells own the values and the times; the paragraph says what happened and who did it. It went from 'You typed Chen-Ito at 9:05. At 9:08 the church office changed the same field to Ito. Your edit went out at 9:12, read their value first and left it alone…' to 'Your correction went out at 9:12 and did not overwrite anything — the church office had already changed the same field. Nothing of yours was written, and nothing of theirs was lost. Which one is right is yours to say.' The two values, the two authors and the two times are now each said exactly once, in the cell built for them; 9:12 stays in the prose because it is the one fact the cells do not hold. Two lines came off the strip — on the phone the record's own actions and the Profile card are back on the fold, where nothing below the strip was before. The left cell's provenance was shortened to 'church office · 9:08' so both cells are one line, one baseline, no dead band.
changes.rationale: Of the three registers the cells are the one that cannot be shortened without losing the comparison, and the buttons are the one that cannot be shortened without losing the round-2 fix that made the choice legible without re-reading. So the paragraph is the one that gives way. This is also the cheapest available height on the tallest object in the record.
changes.breakpoint: both — it is copy, and the same copy at both widths
changes.implementation: `StudentSyncStrip`, `state='differs'`: the body string takes only `sentAt` and `observedActor`; `requestedValue`, `observedValue`, `requestedAt` and `observedAt` are passed to the `<dl>` only. The rule to hold for every state: a value or a timestamp that appears in a cell does not appear in the paragraph.

addresses: MINOR, visual-phone: 'the two buttons have opposite consequences … and they are 44 CSS px tall with 8 CSS px between them, so the brief's own 8px mis-tap lands exactly in the gap and a 10px one lands on the other decision.'
visual-phone: 'Do not re-introduce a weight difference to separate them — that was the round-2 bug.'
changes.change: The strip's action column went `gap-2` → `gap-4 lg:gap-2`: 16 CSS px between 'Keep Ito' and 'Send Chen-Ito again' under a thumb, 8 at a pointer. Nothing else about the pair changed — same fill, same height, same weight, same order. (`.lg\:gap-2` was written into the override block, which is the utility Tailwind would emit.)
changes.rationale: The two goals genuinely conflict here and the answer is the responsive one: separation is a touch problem and buying it on the laptop would only loosen a pair that is meant to read as one question. I took the gap rather than the 48px target because height is what the round-2 fix spent to get both labels to name their value on one line, and because doubling the gap doubles the mis-tap margin at zero cost to either.
changes.breakpoint: below lg — 16px; at lg and up unchanged at 8px
changes.implementation: `StudentSyncStrip`'s actions column is `flex flex-col gap-4 lg:gap-2` wherever the strip offers **two actions with different consequences** (`differs`, `merged`). Where the second action is a retreat rather than an alternative — `orphaned`'s 'Discard the edit', `merged`'s 'Got it' — the existing spacing is fine, but the same class is harmless and keeps one rule.

addresses: MINOR, design-desktop + design-phone: 'Bold is doing two unrelated jobs in one paragraph and the less important job is winning' — a 58-character instruction about where to look is set at the same weight as the two field names, across a line and a half, brighter and bigger than the notice's own heading.
changes.change: The instruction left the paragraph. The body now ends at the fact — '…and it goes out before anything you save. Nothing here is locked, and nothing of his is lost.' — with bold reserved for **Last name** and **Grade**, the two things the reader has to take away. The pointer at the per-field hints dropped to the quiet ink-500 caption rank that sync-blocked's notice already uses for its aside: 'Each of those two boxes says underneath what he is changing it to, and Save sends only the boxes you change.'
changes.rationale: One meaning per weight, and the sibling notice already had the register to move it into, so this is a re-use rather than a new pattern. Keeping the sentence rather than deleting it matters: it is what makes an untouched box safe to leave, and that promise has to be on the glass somewhere. It just does not have to shout.
changes.implementation:
`SyncNotice` takes `body` and an optional `aside`; the aside renders as `

`, the same element sync-blocked's guarantee uses. Bold inside `body` is only ever a field name or an incoming value.

addresses: MINOR, design-phone: 'The two pills that state this journey's whole answer — In flight and Needs you — are adjacent in order and end up at diagonally opposite corners of the block … the pairing the reader is meant to see is the one the wrap breaks.'
design-phone: 'On sync-outage line one holds Incomplete profiles 10 alone … and the alarm the page is about is pushed onto line two. The neutral count gets a line of its own; the red one shares.'
changes.change: The shelf became two groups instead of four loose chips: a job group and a standing group, in that order, inside a container with `gap-x-4 gap-y-2`. Each group is `flex shrink-0 flex-wrap gap-2`, so a group moves to the next line whole rather than being torn in half. On sync-students the phone now reads 'In flight 4 · Needs you 2' on line one and 'Incomplete profiles 10 · Visitors 1' on line two — the pair that answers the screen's question is one line, and the wrap falls between the groups. On sync-outage 'Held by the outage 10' has line one to itself and the two standing counts share line two, which is the reverse of what the critic measured.
changes.rationale: Ordering alone would not have held: flex-wrap fills greedily, so at 390px 'Held by the outage' and 'Incomplete profiles' would still have packed onto one line and split the standing pair instead. Making the grouping structural means the break point is a fact about the content rather than a coincidence of two chip widths, and it survives a count going from 3 to 13. The wider column gap is what makes the grouping legible when both groups do fit on one line, which is the desktop case.
changes.breakpoint: both in markup, visible below lg — at 1440px the shelf sits on one line beside the selects and the group gap simply reads as a gutter between jobs and standing facts
changes.implementation: `StudentsPage` filter shelf: `<div role="group" aria-label="Quick filters" class="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-4 gap-y-2 lg:shrink-0">` containing two `<span class="flex shrink-0 flex-wrap gap-2">` — the first holds the job pills (`In flight`, `Needs you`, or `Held by the outage` while an outage notice is standing), the second the standing pills (`Incomplete profiles`, `Visitors`). New pills go in the group they belong to, never appended to the end.

addresses: MINOR, design-phone: 'the only red marks in the frame sit on two of the fields that are merely waiting, and what they assert is a demand on the reader against controls that refuse input … the sheet marks as required exactly the set she cannot type into.'
changes.change: The required asterisks came off 'First name' and 'Last name' inside the held group, so there is no danger-ramp ink anywhere on a sheet whose whole message is that nothing has failed. They return with the controls when the create lands.
changes.rationale: A requirement marker is a statement about what the reader must supply before submitting, and neither is true of a control that refuses input on a form whose submit button says 'Save notes'. Dropping the marker was cheaper than restating it in the ink ramp and does not lose anything: the group's one sentence already says what these six are and when they come back.
changes.implementation: `FormField` suppresses the `required` marker whenever the control is held, alongside the `aria-describedby` redirect and the `disabled:opacity-100 disabled:text-ink-300` pairing round 2 added. The underlying `required` attribute is irrelevant here — the held fields are not part of the submitted form.

addresses: MINOR, visual-desktop: 'the sentence is written about the admin in the third person … and the branch only swaps the buttons when the reader is the admin. Priya arriving on this screen reads a paragraph telling her that somebody else will fix it, above a settings button.'
MINOR, visual-desktop: 'the frame names the admin Priya Raman and eight rows below carries a student row Priya Raman, 10th grade.'
changes.change: Two things. (1) The hand-off was restructured so the clause that branches on the reader is a single span rather than the whole paragraph, and the sentence now ends on the move this reader's loudest button makes: '…Nothing typed is lost and all ten go out the moment it is back — retrying will not help. **Priya Raman is your admin**, and she is the only person who can reconnect it. These ten are the only records affected.' The bold span is the swap point; for the admin it reads '**You are the only person who can reconnect it** — ten records are waiting on you', which is what pairs with 'Open Planning Center settings' as the primary. (2) The seeded 10th-grader was renamed Priya Raman → **Petra Raman**, keeping the PR initials so nothing else on the row moves.
changes.rationale: The frame stays Dana's, because that is the branch four critics have now read and because core team is the common reader of this screen; switching it to Priya would have un-rendered the validated half and bought a new round of findings on the other. What I could fix on the glass without that cost is the structural one — the sentence used to be written as prose about a third party, which is why only the buttons could branch; it is now one clause in one span, so the copy and the button swap together from one flag. The rename was the whole of the second half.
changes.breakpoint: both — the role branch is a data condition, not a viewport one
changes.implementation: `SyncOutageNotice` renders `body` as `{scale sentence} {reassurance} {handoff} {scope sentence}`, where `handoff` is the only role-dependent string: `viewerIsAdmin ? 'You are the only person who can reconnect it — ' + n + ' records are waiting on you' : admin.name + ' is your admin, and ' + pronoun + ' is the only person who can reconnect it'`. The primary and the ghost swap on the same flag, as round 2 specified — one condition drives both, so they cannot disagree. The `admin` fallback with no admin on the team stays 'Ask an admin to reconnect it' with no action.

addresses: MINOR, design-desktop: 'Two kinds of apostrophe are on the glass at once in the same modal, in the same class of sentence … the three straight ones read as text that came from a different keyboard than everything around it.'
changes.change: The four straight apostrophes on the glass — "Planning Center's" twice in sync-blocked, once in sync-editor, and "Amara's" in the held group's sentence — are curly, matching the rest of the copy. Nothing else changed.
changes.rationale: Cheap and obviously right, and the sort of thing that only gets fixed in a round that has a list.
changes.implementation: Copy strings in `StudentEditorDialog`. Worth a lint rule: no `'` in user-facing English.

declined.finding: MINOR, design-desktop: '‖ renders as a solid vertical bar and ! renders as the same bar with a 2px break — the state that resolves itself and the state that will not are separated by two pixels of counter. Give failed a silhouette with mass.'
declined.why: Declined on this round's instruction not to reopen the mark family, and I think that is right independent of the instruction. Re-cutting a glyph would touch five files and twelve marks — ! carries all ten held rows on sync-outage as well as failed on two record scenes — for a difference the same critic measured at 11px in greyscale with the hue stripped, which is not how either mark is ever read: on every frame the mark carries a word beside it and a colour that already separates warn from danger. Reopening the family in the round that is meant to close the loop is exactly the move that produces a fourth round of new findings. If a later round still wants it, the cheapest honest fix is `!` → a filled triangle, changed in the one `GLYPH` map, and it should be done with the whole family re-shot at once.

declined.finding: MINOR, design-desktop: 'the strip has a measure but no right edge — on sync-outage 407px of the strip is empty over its full height, and on sync-orphaned 155px.'
declined.why: Real, and left. The two ways to close it both cost something the round-2 work bought: pushing the actions to the far edge puts a 480px gutter between a sentence and the button it justifies, which is the trench that finding existed to fill; letting the message give up its cap returns the strip to a 105-character measure on sync-outage. What I did instead is narrower and worth recording: the new merged strip was written so its action column's guard sentence is short enough that the actions do **not** wrap, and it therefore reaches the strip's right edge exactly as `differs`, `failed` and `queued` do. The rule for the implementer is that a guard sentence in the actions column should be under about 40 characters; past that the column wraps and the strip grows a void.

declined.finding: MINOR, design-desktop: 'each glyph-led block has two left edges about 25px apart — the button sits outboard of the paragraph that justifies it, the field labels outboard of the sentence that explains them.'
declined.why: Left this round. It is a real and general fix — treat the glyph as a gutter and indent every sibling to the prose edge — but it is a change to the shared block shell that would move content on six of the nine frames, and it is a minor arriving in the round that should converge. Removing sync-blocked's create button has already halved the instance the critic led with: the notice no longer has an outboard button under it, only prose. The remaining cases are label edges inside the held group and the caption on sync-orphaned. Recorded for the implementation of `SyncNotice`/`StudentSyncStrip`: the glyph belongs in a fixed-width leading gutter that all block children clear, not in the first flex row.

declined.finding: MINOR, design-desktop: 'grade and last-seen right edges take three and four different values down the roster, because a two-chip row pays for itself out of the columns to its left.'
declined.why: Left. The fix — set right edges for grade and last-seen and a floor on the flag cluster sized to its busiest row — is correct and is written down here for the implementer, but it is a third pass at the same row after round 1 built it and round 2 columned its middle band, and every previous pass has moved something a critic then had to re-read. It is also the cheapest of these to do later, because it is two `w-` classes on two flex children and touches no copy: `lg:w-20` on grade (already there), `lg:w-24 lg:text-right` on last-seen, and the flag cluster's `lg:min-w-60` floor raised to its busiest row rather than its median.

declined.finding: MINOR, design-desktop: 'the failure mark is the lightest job mark in the column — give the danger pair a common floor and take the width back off the landed state.'
declined.why: Left, and I am not sure it is right. The proposal is to lengthen '! Save failed · 1wk' and shorten '✓ Saved · just now', but 'just now' is the whole content of the landed mark — it is what tells Dana, mid-run, that the row she saved four seconds ago is done, which is J2's entire question — and a mark that says only 'Saved' cannot answer it. The underlying observation about optical mass is a property of the danger ramp against ink-900, which is a design-system fact rather than a chip fact, and fixing it in the chip would mean a bespoke weight for one state.

declined.finding: MINOR, design-desktop: 'sync-differs has three identical objects — the two halves of the decision and Edit profile — and the choice is laid out on a perpendicular axis to the comparison it resolves. Bind each action to its own cell.'
declined.why: Declined. Putting each button inside its own cell would make the comparison a pair of targets, and the round-2 fix that made this screen safe rests on the values being the figure and the buttons being a matched, separate pair; a value that is also a button is a value you can hit while reading it — on a phone, with 44px rows, on a choice one half of which overwrites a named human's deliberate correction. The axis mismatch is real and is the price of the phone order (question before answer) that the same critique family asked for last round. The second half — stepping 'Edit profile' down when the strip declines to have a primary — I also left, because the rank it would break is the one round 2 set across all four record states ('ink pill when something needs a human'), and having one state disagree with the other three is worse than having three peers on one of them.

declined.finding: visual-phone (minor): the offline branch of the queued strip, and phone renders of `sending` / `waiting`.
declined.why: Declined for the third time, with the phone critic's own verdict this round agreeing they should stay declined. Nothing new to add: the offline wording is specified verbatim in the r01 and r02 records and the implementation must not ship the unconditional 'it goes on its own, even if you lock your phone' clause without the branch.

declined.finding: r01 scope declines: the two-column record at lg, and a wider editor dialog at lg.
declined.why: Not re-filed and not re-argued, per this round's instruction. They stay declined.
